Overview

Each dot is a bundle of traffic (0.1 Gbit), queued and forwarded by a simulated network. Most international traffic goes through a few landing stations on Karachi's coast, then out on submarine cables.

Stories

Borders from Natural Earth; city positions from GeoNames (443 places). Which ISP runs which route isn't public, so the network here is representative, not exact.

Count-to-infinity (real RIP)

One round = RIP's 30-second update, compressed to under a second. Metric: hop count; 16 means unreachable (RFC 2453).

Break something and watch traffic reroute.

Submarine cables

Cable status checked Nov 2026. Africa-1 and 2Africa have landed but aren't confirmed in service; SMW6 is partly active and sources disagree. Hover a cable for details.

Alerts

Run a scenario. Then switch defence off and run it again to compare.

What each network believes ·

Route each network uses for YouTube's address 208.65.153.238 (longest-prefix match). Relationships are CAIDA inferences; world regions are aggregates.

Cable utilisation

Measured from the simulation: bundles of 0.1 Gbit on links with representative capacities, FIFO queues and tail drop. Convergence time is measured for OSPF and RIP, and still mocked for BGP.
